body:
Full spec: .adlc/specs/T47.md — read it first.

GOAL
Vercel AI Gateway is ALREADY a fully supported provider (--provider vercel / gateway, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY or VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN). Nothing needs adding. This ticket fixes a maintainability defect in its default model pins that silently degrades review quality.

PROBLEM 1 — THE SAME MODEL STRINGS ARE HARDCODED IN SIX PLACES ACROSS FOUR SITES in src/llm.js:
  822:  gatewayPreferModel = "openai/gpt-5";
  854:  gatewayPreferModel = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6";
  993:  model = gatewayPreferModel || cfgModel || "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6";
  1070: openai:    "openai/gpt-5",
  1071: anthropic: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6",
  1072: gemini:    "google/gemini-2.5-pro"
GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS (1069-1073) READS LIKE the source of truth but is NOT — lines 822, 854, and 993 each hardcode the same strings independently. Changing the map alone does not change auto-detection behavior.

PROBLEM 2 — THE PINS HAVE DRIFTED. Verified against GET https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models (312 models; endpoint requires NO authentication):
  openai    pinned openai/gpt-5 (ctx 400,000)          -> newest suitable openai/gpt-5.6-sol (ctx 1,050,000). STALE: 5.1 through 5.6 all shipped.
  anthropic pinned anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 (ctx 1,000,000) -> newest suitable anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 (ctx 1,000,000). STALE: a full major generation.
  gemini    pinned google/gemini-2.5-pro (ctx 1,048,576) -> KEEP. See below.
All three pins still resolve, so nothing is currently broken. The harm is quiet: an older reviewer catches fewer bugs and nothing surfaces that fact.

GEMINI DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MOVE. The catalog contains NO stable 3.x pro text model. The 3.x line is gemini-3-flash, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, image variants, and exactly one pro: google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview. Moving off gemini-2.5-pro would mean either dropping to a weaker flash tier or adopting a preview model. Keep the pin and record the reasoning in a code comment so the next reader does not "fix" it.

TIER IS PRESERVED on the pins that move: gpt-5 -> gpt-5.6-sol and claude-sonnet-4.6 -> claude-sonnet-5 each stay in their existing tier rather than jumping to a -pro / -opus tier, so review cost and latency characteristics are unchanged. The openai move also raises the context window 2.6x (400k -> 1.05M), which directly benefits large-diff review.

SOLUTION
1. Make GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS the only place a gateway model id is written; lines 822, 854, 993 read from it.
2. Move the openai and anthropic pins forward; leave gemini pinned with an explanatory comment.
3. Add a catalog drift test against the unauthenticated models endpoint that FAILS when a pin has been REMOVED and REPORTS (without failing) when a newer same-family, same-tier model exists.

THE DRIFT TEST MUST NEVER MAKE npm test DEPEND ON THE NETWORK. It fetches with a short timeout and SKIPS on any network error, non-200, or unparseable body. A missing pin is a real failure; an unreachable Vercel is not.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each maps to a test; see spec for full wording)
AC1  GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS is the single source of truth. No gateway model id literal (openai/..., anthropic/..., google/...) appears anywhere else in src/. Enforced by a test in test/gateway-model-drift.test.mjs that greps src/llm.js and asserts zero matches outside the map definition.
AC2  Ladder assignments at src/llm.js:822 and :854 read GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS.openai and GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS.anthropic rather than literals. Verified in test/llm.test.js by asserting the resolved gatewayPreferModel equals the map value for each ladder branch.
AC3  The fallback default at src/llm.js:993 reads GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS.anthropic rather than a literal. Verified in test/llm-config.test.mjs.
AC4  Pins are openai: "openai/gpt-5.6-sol", anthropic: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5", gemini: "google/gemini-2.5-pro". A code comment above the gemini entry records that no stable 3.x pro text model exists and that gemini-3.1-pro-preview was rejected as a preview. Verified in test/llm.test.js.
AC5  Model precedence unchanged: explicit --model beats gatewayPreferModel, which beats the configured model, which beats the map default. Verified in test/llm-config.test.mjs with a case for each rung.
AC6  Drift test in test/gateway-model-drift.test.mjs fetches https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models with NO auth header and asserts every value in GATEWAY_FAMILY_MODELS is present in the returned data[].id set. A removed pin fails the test.
AC7  The drift test SKIPS rather than FAILS on network error, non-200 status, timeout, or unparseable JSON, and uses a timeout of 15s or less. Verified by injecting a stubbed fetch that throws, one that returns 503, and one that returns malformed JSON — each must skip, not fail. npm test MUST pass with networking disabled.
AC8  The drift test emits a non-failing diagnostic listing newer same-family models present in the catalog but not pinned, so drift is visible without blocking a build. Verified in test/gateway-model-drift.test.mjs with a stubbed catalog containing a newer id.
AC9  The GATEWAY model references in README.md (line 251 default, and the provider/model examples at line 260) reflect the new pins. The NATIVE-API defaults at README.md:247-249 (claude-sonnet-4-6, gemini-2.5-pro, gpt-5) and the config example at README.md:287 are NOT gateway pins and MUST NOT be touched. Verification MUST use fixed-string greps (grep -F): an unescaped grep "claude-sonnet-4.6" ALSO matches the native form claude-sonnet-4-6 at line 247, because . is a wildcard. Verify: grep -cF 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6' README.md returns 0; grep -cF 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5' README.md returns >=1; grep -cF 'openai/gpt-5.6-sol' README.md returns >=1; grep -cF 'google/gemini-2.5-pro' README.md returns >=1 (unchanged); grep -cF 'claude-sonnet-4-6' README.md still returns 1 (native default, deliberately preserved).
AC10 npm test passes, both with and without network access.

VERIFICATION COMMAND
npm test

OUT OF SCOPE
- Adding Vercel AI Gateway as a provider — it already exists and is fully wired.
- Changing the gateway's status as a TRANSPORT rather than a diversity family (src/llm.js:1055). That design is correct and stays.
- Automatically resolving pins at runtime from the catalog. Runtime model selection must stay deterministic and offline-capable; drift detection belongs in tests, not the review path.
- Moving the gemini pin.
title: Collapse Vercel AI Gateway model pins to a single source of truth and detect catalog drift
